page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m1.2xlarge is an x86_64 burstable virtual server instance powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor under KVM hypervisor management. The instance features 4 physical cores supporting Hyper-Threading to deliver 8 vCPUs, paired with 8.0 GB of memory (1.0 GB per vCPU). It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU accelerators, relying on external network storage, and provides a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. Processor instruction set features include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, FMA, BMI2, and ADX.

Performance benchmarks highlight the instance's burstable resource profile. Single-threaded execution yields low throughput, recording a single-core stress-ng score of 1053.09 and a Geekbench single-core score of 809.0. Multi-core compute performance registers at baseline levels, evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng result of 8203.45 and a Passmark CPU score of 9165.89. Memory benchmarks report an uncached read bandwidth of 57.64 GB/sec and a Passmark memory score of 1375.33. Database operations produce 1833.86 in Passmark, while Redis SET throughput reaches 8.4 million operations per second.

The 1:1 RAM-to-vCPU allocation and burstable execution model deliver a cost-efficient resource footprint for non-continuous workloads that do not demand sustained maximum CPU utilization. Primary tradeoffs include constrained single-core CPU speeds and limited memory per core. This configuration aligns with lightweight microservices, software compilation jobs, development sandboxes, low-traffic web serving, and transient background processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m1.2xlarge is a burstable x86_64 server instance equipped with 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of RAM. Managing virtualization through KVM, the instance operates with a 1:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps, without local disk storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate average multi-core CPU capacity, including a Passmark CPU score of 9165.89 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 8203.45, alongside a Redis SET throughput of 8.4 million operations per second. However, single-core execution and memory throughput remain in lower performance tiers. This server configuration offers qualitative cost efficiency for budget-conscious compute tasks that tolerate burstable CPU limits, making it suitable for basic web serving, light CI/CD compilation, developmental sandboxes, and low-concurrency application backends.
